codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of SkillFileWatcher using the watchdog library. The class monitors backend/skills/ directories for changes to manifest.yaml and handler.py files. On change, it validates the manifest via parse_manifest(), invalidates bytecode caches, reloads the handler module through SkillLoader.load(), applies manifest metadata to the skill instance, and updates the SkillRegistry. Invalid changes (bad manifest, broken handler, missing files) are caught and logged without crashing the watcher. The watcher integrates correctly into main.py's lifespan (start on startup, stop on shutdown) as a background daemon thread. Debounce prevents rapid-fire events. 25 comprehensive tests all pass covering init, manifest/handler reload, file detection, error handling, registry integration, brain tool loop, debounce, and set_registry. The Brain's tool loop picks up reloaded skills automatically because the watcher updates the same SkillRegistry instance.

issues.description: The _reload_skill_sync method uses asyncio.get_running_loop() to detect if it's inside an async context, then calls run_coroutine_threadsafe().result(timeout=30). Since this runs in a watchdog-spawned daemon thread, there is typically no running loop in that thread, so it always falls through to asyncio.run(). The run_coroutine_threadsafe path would only activate during tests or unusual threading scenarios. This is not a bug but the branching logic could be simplified since the production path always uses asyncio.run().

In _schedule_reload(), if both manifest.yaml and handler.py change simultaneously (e.g., during a git checkout), only the first file event triggers a reload due to per-skill debounce. The second file's change is silently dropped. This is acceptable since the reload processes both files regardless of which one triggered it, but it could be confusing if someone edits only handler.py right after editing manifest.yaml within the debounce window.

After a failed reload (e.g., broken handler), the previous working version of the skill remains in the registry. This is sensible 'last known good' behavior but is not explicitly documented in the class docstring. Could cause confusion if operators expect a failed reload to disable the skill.

summary: The skill-hot-reload feature is correctly implemented. SkillFileWatcher uses the watchdog library to monitor backend/skills/ for changes to manifest.yaml and handler.py files. On detected changes, it validates manifests, reloads handler modules (with bytecode cache invalidation), and updates the skill registry. Error handling is robust — invalid manifests, broken handlers, and missing files are all caught and logged without crashing the watcher. The watcher starts as a daemon thread during app startup and stops on shutdown, integrated into main.py's lifespan. All 25 tests pass, covering initialization, manifest/handler reload paths, file detection, error cases, registry integration, brain tool loop integration, debounce, and registry switching. The only notable discrepancy is the handoff metadata referencing the wrong commitId (calendar commit instead of hot-reload commit), but the actual code is correct.
